title: Hoopaninak
summary: Hoopaninak is recorded by William Wallace Tooker as an island at Flatlands in Kings County. The name appears in a 1664 deed for upland, marshes, beaches, and an adjoining island described as enclosed by the ocean sea.
map_geometry_source: Approximate general marker for an island at Flatlands described in the 1664 deed cited by Tooker; exact historic island and shoreline need review. Offset from Equendito/Barren Island for map visibility.
translation_content:
The name is interpreted as the enclosed or shut-in island-place, through roots meaning to enclose or shut in joined with a word for island place.

Why Place Names Matter

“Today, many indigenous people around the world are reclaiming their original place names and returning them back to the maps. This process is aiding in the preservation and protection of cultural heritage.”

— Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park, Restoration of Indigenous Place Names (2021), Audio transcript
land_loss_content: Hoopaninak preserves a name for an island and marsh landscape that has been reshaped by coastal change, filling, and modern infrastructure. Mapping it approximately keeps the deed language visible without pretending the historic island can yet be placed exactly.
whereintheworld_content: The map placement is an approximate general point for the historical Flatlands/Jamaica Bay island landscape. The exact island has not been matched to a modern shoreline, and the point is offset from nearby Barren Island-related records for map visibility.
